_note: report-strategic's checked-in routing corpus — the test of record. Positives are real requests for a formal STRATEGIC report / strategy brief: a self-contained document that establishes shared vocabulary (glossary) and context BEFORE analysis, then delivers findings with evidence and prioritized strategic RECOMMENDATIONS with owners + success conditions + a bibliography, for a mixed (exec + technical) audience. Negatives are drawn ADVERSARIALLY from the three near-synonymous report-* siblings — a CIA-style intel BRIEF for rapid knowledge transfer (BLUF/confidence/intel-gaps, no recommendations) is report-brief; a bounded project's PROGRESS / STATUS over a period is report-progress; a comprehensive current-STATE / situation snapshot is report-state — plus resume-author. The hard boundary is report-brief: both can be called a 'brief', but strategic = context-setting + recommendations document; brief = dense confidence-annotated knowledge transfer with no recommendations. Each negative belongs to a NAMED sibling. routing-eval is lexical-overlap only; the shared 'brief'/'strategy' tokens make some report-brief overlap a proxy limit, not a defect.
